abstract.p: We show that a tiny Co 4 machine (Adeel, 2025) with a single layer, two heads, and 8M parameters, operating at an approximate cost of O(N) (where N is the number of input tokens), outpaces the BabyLM Challenge baselines GPT-2 1 (124M, 12 layers, O(N 2)) and GPT-BERT 2 (30M, 12 layers, O(N 2)) in just two epochs, while both are trained for ten. Co 4 achieves orders-of-magnitude greater training efficiency on 10M tokens, demonstrating highly sampleefficient pretraining. Using the BabyLM challenge evaluation pipeline across complex benchmarks, Co 4 exhibits strong zero-shot and fine-tuning performance on SuperGLUE tasks. Specifically, Co 4 outperforms GPT-2 on 5 out of 7 zero-shot metrics and 6 out of 7 fine-tuning tasks, and GPT-BERT on 4 out of 7 metrics in both cases. These results suggest the need to rethink prevailing deep learning paradigms and associated scaling laws.
